label: Copy-phase update gate: short-sequence copy steps and r/h/f/3/x echo inputs
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L, never in the original or delimiter steps, and never when the input is a first occurrence, since copy inputs repeat original tokens). The strongest activations are in very short sequences: for L=3 it is active on almost every copy step (precision 0.99), peaking at the last step (recall_idx 2), where the max is about 0.039; for L=4 it fires mainly at recall_idx 2 (precision 0.67). In longer sequences it fires more weakly and diffusely across mid-to-late copy steps (recall_idx 2-5, to_go <= 5), and more often when the fed-back input is r, h, f, 3 or x (rate 11-20% vs a 12% copy-phase base). The predicate covers about 81% of activation mass but precision is about 0.40; many weaker activations in long sequences on other tokens are not captured by any simple condition I tested.
